title: Stability, Qualitative Dynamics and Bifurcations
description: Equilibria, Lyapunov stability, LaSalle invariance, Hartman-Grobman, limit cycles, and Hamiltonian dynamics (E01-E14)

declarations.name: Equilibria, Invariant Sets and Omega-Limit Sets
declarations.scope_summary: Dynamical systems on R^n or manifolds
declarations.statement_summary: Equilibrium points f(x*) = 0; positively invariant sets Phi^t(S) subset S for t >= 0; omega-limit set omega(x).

declarations.name: Lyapunov, Asymptotic and Exponential Stability
declarations.scope_summary: Equilibrium x* under perturbation epsilon/delta bounds
declarations.statement_summary: Stable if for all eps > 0 exists delta > 0 such that ||x0 - x*|| < delta implies ||Phi^t(x0) - x*|| < eps for all t >= 0.

declarations.name: Linear Stability and Spectral Abscissa
declarations.statement_summary: 0 is exponentially stable iff all eigenvalues of A have strictly negative real parts: max Re lambda_i < 0.

declarations.name: Lyapunov Indirect Method (Linearized Stability)
declarations.scope_summary: Hyperbolic equilibria with Jacobian matrix A = Df(x*)
declarations.statement_summary: If all eigenvalues of A have Re lambda < 0, x* is exponentially stable for the nonlinear system x' = f(x).

declarations.name: Lyapunov Direct Method and Energy Sublevel Sets
declarations.statement_summary: If V'(x) = grad(V)(x) . f(x) <= 0, x* is stable; if V'(x) < 0 for x != x*, x* is asymptotically stable.

declarations.name: LaSalle Invariance Principle and Attracting Sets
declarations.scope_summary: Compact positively invariant set Omega with V'(x) <= 0
declarations.statement_summary: Every trajectory in Omega approaches the largest invariant subset M of {x in Omega : V'(x) = 0} as t -> infty.

declarations.name: Hartman-Grobman Linearization and Invariant Manifolds
declarations.scope_summary: Hyperbolic equilibrium points (no eigenvalues with Re lambda = 0)
declarations.statement_summary: The nonlinear flow is locally topologically conjugate to the linear flow x' = Df(x*) x; exists stable/unstable C^k manifolds W^s, W^u.

declarations.name: Phase Planes, Nullclines and Poincaré Return Maps
declarations.scope_summary: Planar dynamical systems and transversal cross-sections
declarations.statement_summary: Nullcline curves x' = 0, y' = 0; Poincaré first return map P: Sigma -> Sigma with return time tau(x).

declarations.name: Poincaré-Bendixson Theorem and Bendixson-Dulac Criterion
declarations.scope_summary: Planar C^1 autonomous vector fields in R^2
declarations.statement_summary: A compact limit set containing no equilibria is a periodic orbit; Bendixson-Dulac divergence condition rules out closed orbits.

declarations.name: Periodic Orbit Stability and Characteristic Multipliers
declarations.scope_summary: Periodic orbits gamma(t) of autonomous systems
declarations.statement_summary: One Floquet multiplier is always 1 (tangential shift); orbit is asymptotically stable if all remaining multipliers have |mu_i| < 1.

declarations.name: Local Bifurcations and Center Manifold Reduction
declarations.statement_summary: Saddle-node, transcritical, pitchfork, and Hopf bifurcations classified via center manifold reduction.

declarations.name: Gradient and Hamiltonian Flows and Conservation Laws
declarations.scope_summary: Gradient systems x' = -grad V(x) vs Hamiltonian systems q' = partial_p H, p' = -partial_q H
declarations.statement_summary: Gradient flows monotonically decrease energy; Hamiltonian flows preserve energy H(q,p) = const and symplectic phase volume.

declarations.name: Liouville-Arnold Integrability and Action-Angle Coordinates
declarations.scope_summary: Hamiltonian systems with n independent first integrals in involution
declarations.statement_summary: Compact connected regular invariant level sets are n-dimensional tori T^n with quasi-periodic linear flows in action-angle variables.

declarations.name: Smale Horseshoes, Chaos and Lyapunov Exponents
declarations.scope_summary: Deterministic nonlinear dynamical systems with sensitive initial conditions
declarations.statement_summary: Maximal Lyapunov exponent lambda = lim (1/t) ln(||delta x(t)|| / ||delta x(0)||) > 0 indicates exponential divergence and chaos.
